title: Contract Clause Library: Escrow, KMS, Data Residency, and Billing Flags
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview:
This document is a consolidated clause library and operational playbook intended for use by finance, legal, procurement, and sales teams when negotiating or approving customer contracts with technical controls or billing impacts. It captures recommended contract language for: escrow and code escrow triggers, key management (KMS/HSM) obligations, data residency and processing location restrictions, and billing flags that affect revenue recognition and invoicing cadence. The goal is consistent, auditable contract language that minimizes downstream revrec complexity and procurement friction.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Customer and reseller contracts for Redwood Inference product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private). Includes SOWs and addenda that change revenue timing, invoicing, or technical controls.
- Primary audience: Finance, Legal, Procurement, Sales enablement, Account Executives, Solutions Engineering.
- Secondary audience: Security & Compliance, Product, Customer Success.

Owners and escalation paths:
- Clause library owner: Finance-Legal (Asha Patel).
- Legal drafter for exceptions: Senior Counsel (Diego Morales).
- RevRec reviewer: Revenue Accounting lead (Jane Kim).
- Security reviewer (data/KMS/escrow): Head of Security Compliance (Omar Rashid).
- Procurement intake: Procurement Manager (name as assigned).
- Escalation: If a clause causes >$500k ARR deferral or increases implementation effort > 3 FTE-weeks, escalate to VP Finance + General Counsel.

How to use this page (quickstart):
1) Determine which product(s) are in scope (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
2) Identify requested clauses from customer (e.g., data residency to EU, KMS BYOK, code escrow).
3) Consult the clause catalog below and copy the recommended language.
4) Route drafted clause to reviewers: Legal -> Security -> RevRec (target turnaround 5 business days).
5) If clause alters invoicing cadence or creates collectability/performance conditions, flag RevRec and set billing_flag (see Billing Flags table).

Clause catalog (recommended language snippets):
- Data Residency (Standard - EU-only):
  "Customer Data shall be processed and stored exclusively within the European Economic Area (EEA). Redwood will not transfer Customer Data outside the EEA except as required for lawful purposes, and only to recipients subject to an adequacy decision or Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). Redwood will provide region-specific deployment documentation on request."

- Data Residency (Hybrid - EU primary, US DR):
  "Primary processing and storage of Customer Data will occur in the EEA. Redwood may process or store copies of Customer Data in the United States solely for Disaster Recovery (DR) or system resilience, and such processing will be subject to SCCs and Redwood’s technical and organizational controls."

- BYOK KMS (Customer-managed keys):
  "For Private deployments, Customer may supply their own encryption keys (BYOK) managed in Customer’s KMS/HSM. Redwood will integrate with the supplied KMS endpoints and will not retain plaintext keys. Operational runbooks describing key rotation and emergency key access will be agreed in the SOW. Any KMS integration work is billable and will be captured in the implementation SOW."

- Managed KMS (Redwood):
  "Where Customer elects Redwood-managed keys, Redwood will manage cryptographic keys in a customer-dedicated KMS instance. Redwood will provide key rotation logs and KMS audit records for a period of 12 months upon Customer request."

- Code Escrow (recommended threshold):
  "Code escrow will be included for Dedicated or Private contracts where (a) the total committed contract value over the initial term is greater than USD 1,000,000, or (b) regulatory requirement exists. Escrow will be held with an industry-standard escrow agent and triggered on Bankruptcy, Insolvency, Material Breach (uncured for 60 days), or a prolonged service outage defined as failure to meet SLA for 45 consecutive days."

- Escrow Trigger Addendum (service outage):
  "A ‘Prolonged Service Outage’ is defined as failure to meet the applicable SLA (99.9% uptime) for any consecutive 45-day period. Upon trigger, Redwood will provide the escrowed materials subject to the escrow agreement terms."

Billing flags and revrec impact (operational mapping):
Use these flags when proposals or negotiated contracts modify invoicing cadence, deliverable acceptance, or introduce significant upfront implementation services. Tag contracts in the CLM system with the appropriate billing_flag so RevRec automation can apply the correct revenue treatment.

| Billing Flag | Description | RevRec Impact | Finance Approver Threshold |
|-------------|-------------|---------------|---------------------------|
| prepay_nonref | Customer prepays subscription and requests non-refundable credit | Defer revenue to term; recognize ratably unless implementation performance obligations exist | > $250k routed to Director RevRec |
| milestone_controlled | Customer requires acceptance milestones for product functionality | Revenue recognized on milestone completion; requires SOW-level deliverables mapping | Any change > 90 days to standard term must be reviewed by RevRec lead |
| implementation_billable | Paid implementation services (professional services) separate from subscription | Recognize as services revenue per ASC606; ensure separate invoicing | PO or SOW value > $50k requires Procurement review |
| byok_integration | BYOK/KMS workbillable or creates ongoing support costs | If integration requires > 40 hours of engineering, allocate to implementation_billable | > $75k escalation to VP Finance |
| time_and_materials | T&M engagements for integration/support | Recognize as services when performed; ensure hourly rates documented | T&M not to exceed 6 months without Procurement approval |

(Represent above as table in CLM; include billing_flag field on contract metadata.)

Procurement triggers and thresholds (standardized approvals):
1) Non-standard clause that materially affects revenue timing or product scope (billing_flag present) -> Procurement + RevRec + Legal review (SLAT 5 business days).
2) Implementation or onboarding fees > $50k -> require Procurement sign-off and PO.
3) Multi-year or prepaid agreements > $250k ARR -> require Director Finance approval.
4) On-prem/private deployments requiring hardware purchases or third-party licenses -> Procurement-led sourcing and vendor evaluation.

Contract lifecycle checklist (recommended routing):
1) AE/SE drafts proposal -> include clause selections from this library.
2) Legal: initial redline using recommended language (T+2 business days).
3) Security & Compliance: review data/KMS/escrow language (T+3 business days).
4) RevRec: assess billing_flag and revrec impact (T+5 business days).
5) Procurement: review if hardware/licenses/implementation > threshold.
6) Final sign-off: Countersign by authorized signatory; file in CLM and tag billing_flag.

Revenue recognition rules (summary guidance):
- Subscription licensing (Hosted API): Recognize ratably over the contracted term unless acceptance criteria or milestones alter performance obligations.
- Dedicated capacity: Treat as subscription if access and capacity are transferred; if dedicated setup requires significant customization, split contract lines between subscription and implementation services.
- Private/on-prem: If transfer of control occurs at delivery and customer has significant acceptance testing, consider partial recognition on delivery with remainder upon acceptance.
- Prepayments: Record as deferred revenue and amortize over service period absent separate performance obligations.
- Material modifications (e.g., change of scope or term): Re-evaluate accounting treatment per ASC606 (contract modification) and consult RevRec lead.

Template language examples (short snippets for insertion):
- Implementation SOW billing: "Implementation services will be invoiced per the SOW milestones. Unless otherwise specified, implementation invoices are due within 30 days of invoice and recognized as services revenue upon completion of the milestone deliverable."
- Refund/credit language: "Prepaid subscription fees are non-refundable except as required by applicable law. Refunds or credits for service outages are governed by the SLA."

Recordkeeping and evidence for audits:
- For data residency/KMS clauses: store architecture diagrams, deployment region records, and KMS audit logs for 36 months.
- For escrow: keep executed escrow agreement and trigger correspondence in CLM.
- For billings flagged prepay_nonref or milestone_controlled: retain signed SOW, invoicing schedule, and evidence of milestone completion.

Operational playbooks (integration with systems):
- CLM metadata: Add fields billing_flag, data_residency_region, kms_type (redwood/byok), escrow_required (true/false), implementation_value. Populate these at contract creation.
- Billing system: Map billing_flag to revenue recognition rules and invoice templates. Example mapping: prepay_nonref -> DeferredRevenueSchedule A; milestone_controlled -> RevenueRecognitionRule B.
- Ticketing: If byok_integration selected, create a JIRA epic with label BYOK-{contract_id} and link to SOW.

Change control and exceptions:
- Exceptions to library language require documented business justification and must be approved by Legal + RevRec + Security. Capture approvals in CLM comments.
- Emergency exceptions (customer regulatory deadline within 30 days): Legal to triage within 48 hours and provide redline; RevRec to provide temporary accounting impact memo.

Training and rollout:
- Sales enablement deck with clause highlights and redlines (quarterly).
- RevRec and Procurement office hours monthly for high-touch deals.
- Required reading for AEs in onboarding: this clause library + the RevRec Policy doc.

Appendix A — Example clause: Escrow and DR (full text):
"Escrow Materials" means the source code, build scripts, and documentation required to build and operate the Software. Escrow shall be provided to an independent escrow agent within 60 days of contract signature where the threshold conditions in this library are met. Escrow will be released only upon demonstration of a Triggering Event (Bankruptcy, Insolvency, Material Breach uncured for 60 days, or Prolonged Service Outage). Redwood’s proprietary monitoring and remediation processes shall continue during any escrow release process, and Redwood retains the right to cure any alleged Triggering Event prior to distribution of Escrow Materials as specified in the escrow agreement.

Appendix B — Quick decision matrix (one-page view):
- Does the customer request data residency? -> Yes: select Standard or Hybrid clause and tag data_residency_region. Notify Security.
- Does customer request BYOK? -> Yes: tag byok_integration and estimate engineering hours; if > 40h, create implementation_billable.
- Is total committed value > $1M for Dedicated/Private? -> Yes: consider escrow_required=true and route to VP Finance.
- Does the contract change invoicing or create milestones? -> Yes: tag billing_flag and route to RevRec.
